title: Do Disclosed Safety Evaluations Actually Report Negative Results?

original_idea.body: Do Disclosed Safety Evaluations Actually Report Negative Results?

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Publication-bias finding informs reliance on cards but the chain to catastrophic-risk reduction has a gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Corpus of public cards + LLM classification + hand-labeled validation; beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (negative-result disclosure rate) with validation set; few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Diffuse fuzzy-reward audit of disclosure bias labs won't self-produce; public sources only.

novelty.reasoning: Disclosure scoring exists but the negative-results/publication-bias angle is likely open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Card transparency studied; publication-bias-in-safety-evals angle may be open.
